title: Personal Credit Cards: Minimum Payment, Due Date and Minimum Interest Figures
content:
The following figures shape each monthly statement on Personal Credit Cards: the percentage of the new balance built into the minimum payment, the smallest minimum payment, the number of calendar days from statement closing to the payment due date, and the smallest interest charge billed in a cycle that bears any interest.

| Tier | Share of the new statement balance in the minimum payment | Smallest minimum payment | Calendar days from statement close to due date | Smallest interest charge in a cycle with interest |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secured Visa | 1.00 percent | 25.00 USD | 25 | 1.00 USD |
| College Rewards Visa | 1.00 percent | 25.00 USD | 25 | 0.50 USD |
| Platinum Low Rate Visa | 1.00 percent | 35.00 USD | 25 | 1.00 USD |
| Cash Rewards Visa | 1.00 percent | 35.00 USD | 25 | 1.00 USD |
| Travel Rewards Visa Signature | 1.00 percent | 35.00 USD | 25 | 1.00 USD |
| Visa Infinite Private Client | 1.00 percent | 35.00 USD | 25 | 0.00 USD |

## Points of judgement

- The smallest minimum payment gives way when the statement balance itself is lower; the minimum can never exceed the statement balance.
- On Visa Infinite Private Client the smallest interest charge is 0.00 USD, so a cycle's interest is billed at whatever it actually comes to.

> Hypothetical illustration: a statement on a Cash Rewards Visa account closes on the 4th of a month; counting 25 calendar days from that closing date puts the due date on the 29th of the same month.
